clue.text: Cornish region perhaps welcoming to store?

indicators.note: a host welcoming a guest takes them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Cornwall lies in the South West of England, abbreviated SW
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether some part of Cornwall is happy to act as a storage spot.
explanation.walkthrough: SW (South West) is the region of England that contains Cornwall; the 'perhaps' flags it as one example of what it covers.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow something is to pack it away, a direct verb synonym for putting goods into storage.

clue.text: John, a vagrant in resort for bombing enemy within

indicators.note: a vagrant wanders about, so the letters of the name and article stray into a new order
bombing suggests smashing things up, so the resort's letters are blown apart and rearranged too

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tramp called John turns up at a seaside resort, apparently planning an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: All three pieces are mixed together; 'in' just links the tramp to the resort.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden horse let Greek soldiers into Troy, so the phrase now names any saboteur or subversive element working from inside.

clue.text: Come to steal from elected lords and ladies?

parts.note: to come to is to wake up after being unconscious
to rob is to steal from someone
a candidate who is elected is in office

explanation.surface: Waking up only to rob the newly elected aristocracy of the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: Lords-and-ladies is the cuckoo-pint, a woodland arum plant; 'lords and ladies' looks like the peerage, which is the misdirection. The question mark marks it as an example name.
explanation.definitionFit: Wake-robin is an alternative common name for the wild arum plant also known as lords-and-ladies or cuckoo-pint.

clue.text: Doctor Braille, then married, embodying one's belief

indicators.note: to embody is to contain within a body, so the next piece sits inside the rest
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of the name are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
one's read as 'one is', giving I (one) and S

explanation.surface: A medical doctor called Braille gets married and holds firm to their personal creed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a title before the name Braille, but it is the anagram signal. 'one's' reads as I'S, roman one plus the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberalism is a political creed or philosophy, so it is one kind of belief system someone can hold.

clue.text: Hide ecstasy in panic

indicators.note: the drug sits in the word for panic, placed inside it

parts.note: to be in a lather is to be agitated or flustered
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone tries to conceal their ecstasy pills while in a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb (conceal) but is the noun: an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather is tanned animal skin, and a hide is the skin of an animal, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: He questioned large Northumbrian maybe storing resin used by fuel firm

indicators.note: to store something is to keep it inside, so the resin and firm go within

parts.note: big means large

indicators.note: the resin is followed by, as if used by, the fuel company

parts.note: amber is fossilised tree resin
a gas company, abbreviated GAS CO
Northumberland is in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: A big man from England's north-east keeps resin handy for a fuel company.
explanation.walkthrough: Bamber Gascoigne was the long-serving quizmaster of the British TV show University Challenge, hence 'He questioned'. The large North-Easterner also hints at the footballer Paul Gascoigne.
explanation.definitionFit: As host of a TV quiz show for over twenty years, his job was asking students the questions.

clue.text: Asian ready to call colossus hides a note

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone

indicators.note: hiding the letters puts them out of sight, so they are removed from the word

parts.note: a colossus is a giant
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to phone a huge figure who is concealing a written message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is the noun: ready money, cash. 'n.' is the standard abbreviation for note, as in footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringgit is the currency of Malaysia, and 'the ready' is informal for cash, so it is Asian money.

clue.text: The writer is a good one, but not on metaphor

parts.note: the writer is the setter, who would say I'M
taken as written

indicators.note: but not signals that the following word is dropped from the one before

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer modestly claims to be good, though not at using metaphor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is the setter, so 'The writer is' becomes I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: An image in literature is a figure of speech such as a metaphor or simile, so it covers that sense.

clue.text: Attempt to block chimney erected for tycoon

indicators.note: erected means set upright, so in a down clue the letters read upwards
something placed to block a flue sits inside it

parts.note: lum is the Scottish word for a chimney
to have a go is to make an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone tries to block up a chimney built for a business magnate.
explanation.walkthrough: LUM is Scots for chimney; it reads bottom to top in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A mogul is a powerful magnate, after the Mughal emperors, so it means a wealthy business boss.

clue.text: Fish and chopped nut served on ice

indicators.note: the nut comes on, after, the ice in this across answer

parts.note: a drink on the rocks is served over ice

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an almond is a nut

explanation.surface: A dessert of fish with chopped nuts presented on ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopped' looks like a cooking instruction, but it cuts the nut short by its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock salmon is a British fishmonger's name for dogfish or similar fish sold as food.

clue.text: Witch for strangling knight put to death

indicators.note: strangling grips round the throat, so the outer word encloses the other

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old witch
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A witch is executed for strangling a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang someone is to execute them by the noose, so it is one way of putting a person to death.

clue.text: Eucalyptus in pot starts to reach amazing height

parts.note: a jar is a pot or container

indicators.note: the starts of the words, their opening letters, are taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A potted gum tree shoots up to a remarkable height.
explanation.definitionFit: Jarrah is a Western Australian species of eucalyptus tree, prized for its hard red timber.

clue.text: Covering layers produce paint finish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the shell around eggs, the produce of laying hens
second meaning: a paint with a slight sheen, between matt and gloss

explanation.walkthrough: 'Layers' are laying hens, not coats of paint, and 'produce' is a noun: what they produce is eggs, whose covering is the shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell names both the hard casing of an egg and a low-sheen decorator's paint resembling it.

clue.text: Marine provided with defence against vampire attack?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a US Marine, from the leather collar of the old uniform

definitions.text: provided with defence against vampire attack?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: having a neck covered in leather, so fangs cannot bite through

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful literal reading of the word: a neck of leather would stop a vampire's bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Leatherneck is informal for a member of the US Marine Corps, from the stiff leather stock once worn.

clue.text: Hour taken to feed young bear fish

indicators.note: food is taken into the mouth, so the hour goes inside the young animal

parts.note: a cub is a young bear

explanation.surface: It takes an hour to feed a fish to a bear cub.
explanation.definitionFit: The chub is a freshwater fish of the carp family, common in European rivers.

clue.text: Okay method to adopt following footpath

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the pieces take another inside them

parts.note: righto is a chirpy British way of saying okay
a way is a method

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to take on a method after following a path.
explanation.walkthrough: RIGHTO is informal British for okay; F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in 'pp. 10f'.
explanation.definitionFit: A right of way is a legal path across private land, so it often takes the form of a public footpath.

clue.text: Only slim hope with this paradoxically?

definitions.meaning: the plain meaning: very little chance of something happening
the joke: the phrase meaning slim hope begins with the opposite of slim, a paradox

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is ironic: it says the chance is large while meaning it is tiny, and 'slim' is the antonym of its first word.
explanation.definitionFit: This sarcastic idiom means there is very little likelihood, the opposite of what its words literally say.

clue.text: Given new pitch son departs to play

indicators.note: letters at play move about freely, so these are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A son leaves the stage to perform in a show staged at a new venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests a playing field or a sales pitch; here it is musical pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Music that is transposed is moved into a different key, so its pitch is raised or lowered.

clue.text: Scathingly review article on Rex cat

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece on another sits above it, so the article is placed above the king

parts.note: to pan a show is to slate it
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A critic savages a piece written about Rex the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for Rex, Latin for king, as in royal signatures.
explanation.definitionFit: A panther is a big cat, a leopard or jaguar, especially one with a black coat.

clue.text: Showcase at low volume in underworld ballad

indicators.note: the soft sign sits in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
a lay is a narrative poem or ballad
p (piano) is the musical marking for playing softly

explanation.surface: A ballad about the underworld, sung softly, is put on show.
explanation.walkthrough: DIS is the Roman underworld; p for piano is the musical marking for soft.
explanation.definitionFit: To display something is to exhibit it prominently, the same sense as to showcase it.

clue.text: Something like a goat seen in Utah ranch

indicators.note: the animal is seen inside the run of letters across these two words

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal resembling a goat spotted on a ranch in Utah.
explanation.definitionFit: The tahr is a wild Himalayan mammal related to the goat, a goat-antelope with a shaggy coat.

clue.text: Singing hypocritical words, outwardly mostly inferior

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so the shortened word wraps the other
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: below means inferior, lower in rank
cant is insincere, hypocritical talk

explanation.surface: Someone's singing is dismissed as hypocritical and, on the surface, fairly poor.
explanation.walkthrough: Bel canto, Italian for 'beautiful singing', is the operatic style of smooth, lyrical vocal technique.
explanation.definitionFit: Bel canto is a style of operatic vocal performance with a pure, even tone, so a kind of singing.

clue.text: Resolutely oppose woman out with gay man

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to confront them boldly
second meaning: slang for a woman who dates a closeted gay man as cover

explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like coming out, but here it just means out on a date in public.
explanation.definitionFit: To beard a lion in its den is to defy it; separately a beard is a companion who disguises someone's sexuality.

clue.text: Shoot up at court before campaign

parts.note: in tennis a lob is a shot sent high over the opponent
by means before, as in 'by Friday'

explanation.surface: A tennis player sends the ball high before starting a campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot up' sounds like drugs; the court is a tennis court, and the shot goes up as a lob.
explanation.definitionFit: To lobby is to campaign by pressing politicians or officials to support a cause.

clue.text: Latest information — take this for class

parts.note: the SP, from racing's starting price, is slang for the latest news
'here' is said when handing something over: here, take this

explanation.surface: Someone passes on up-to-date news with a handout for their class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The SP' is British slang for the inside information, from a racehorse's starting price.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere can mean a social stratum or rank, someone's station in life, a sense close to social class.

clue.text: Macho man unable to open reading desk

indicators.note: not able to open, the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: Rambo is the muscle-bound action hero of the Sylvester Stallone films

explanation.surface: A tough guy can't get a reading desk open.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambo is a raised pulpit or lectern in early Christian churches, from which scripture is read.

clue.text: Scottish soldier bombed German states

parts.note: bombed is slang for drunk or high on drugs
Länder are the federal states of Germany

explanation.surface: A Highland soldier carried out bombing raids on German territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bombed' looks like the military action, but it is the slang for intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highlander is a soldier in one of the Highland regiments of the British Army.

clue.text: Care centre with no overnight charges?

definitions.meaning: the plain meaning: a place that looks after young children
charges are the children in its care, none of whom stays the night

explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' looks like fees, but it means children in someone's charge; this place only has them in the daytime.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery that cares for small children only during the working day, sending them home in the evening.

clue.text: Moose have small, black, lustrous tails

indicators.note: the tails of the words are their final letters, which are taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Moose are said to have little shiny black tails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moose' is plural here, matching the plural answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elk is the British name for the animal North Americans call moose, the largest deer.
